steps.name: Terrified Mafioso
steps.text: You sent for me, Don Venezia?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Anton has a question for you.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Over here, Carle.

steps.name: Terrified Mafioso
steps.text: Antonio...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Any cars headed towards Sicilia recently?

steps.name: Terrified Mafioso
steps.text: Passenger routes are operating as usual. Though, most people are coming in here, and not out.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Go pack up your belongings. You should be able to make the last ride over.

steps.name: Terrified Mafioso
steps.text: Gotcha—

steps.name: Terrified Mafioso
steps.text: Uh, Huh? Antonio, what's the meaning of this?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Don't you have a fratello in Sicilia? You can't stay in Nuova Volsinii any longer, and can't go back to Montelupe either, so you should go to him.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Your negligence has caused us to lose a whole carload of 'tires'.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I gave you a chance. Just greet the don at the port, couldn't even manage that. That old Saluzzo stronzo even got to meet papa before you did.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Carle, I've already given you the most decent ending possible by letting you leave, alive. Take this—
A check from a bank, with a huge sum written on it.
The famiglia associate takes it, stunned. He sees his own name written on the upper left, already crossed out by Antonio himself.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Call it a settlement fee. Without the famiglia's protection, you'll need a lot of money.

steps.name: Terrified Mafioso
steps.text: I've been with the Venezias for more than a decade. I was following the Don before you even came in here, can't you just, for his sake—

steps.name: Terrified Mafioso
steps.text: D-Don Venezia—!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Employees who make mistakes must naturally be punished, yes?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Of course. You're the head of Venezia Trucking. You call the shots.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Anton... you didn't inform me about this in advance.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Please don't blame me for this.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The police were just here earlier. They wanted to inspect the vehicle factories and service stations under the Venezia name. They said it was just a routine inspection before Carnevale, but the official warrant said it was an impromptu check.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I also just received news that Alberto was suddenly temporarily detained for corporate qualification issues.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I have no doubt the trial this morning has upset our dear judge Lavinia. She's hoping to control a situation she knows nothing of this way.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The situation spiraled out of my control, so I had to deal with Carle like that. It'll be hard to convince the masses otherwise.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: This year, Venezia Trucking has carefully complied with the New Urban Management Act, and the only clue we had proving otherwise was burned to cinders yesterday at the port.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The only person who can affect our business has been dealt with.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: But when Carnevale is over and Lavinia has her hands free, I'm afraid she'll try her best to target us.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: How do you plan on handling it?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: My original idea was to slowly transform this city—Let it have a set of laws absent in other cities, while establishing an underground order the Siracusans are accustomed to.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Venezia Trucking's business has been smooth sailing. The trick is to follow these two tenets: Comply with the New Urban Management Act, but also not.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Of course, the other famiglie are doing the same, but adapting to the rules of the new game is quite difficult.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The Venezias can fit perfectly into both sets of laws, and we've been excelling at it.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: So much so that today we can discard one and switch to the other immediately.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: So you want to completely control this city?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: You've lost yourself, Anton. Don't forget Nuova Volsinii has Signora Sicilia's endorsement. She supports the youths' reforms.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: You're openly defying her authority and turning us against all of Siracusa this way. You're using the entire Famiglia Venezia as your betting chip!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: It sounds like that, yes.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: The last one to do that was Bernardo... he only died last year!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Are you afraid of Signora Sicilia, afraid of the youngsters at City Hall yelling their ideals across the room?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: You've really gotten old, papa.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: We Venezias hold a most unusual seat in the Grey Hall, a 'hybrid' famiglia. Lupos with no blood ties who left their previous pack, Vulpos like Ingrid, and Perros like you...

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: The other famiglie don't think too kindly of us, but we stand here today nonetheless. Our presence here embodies every Venezia's sweat and blood.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Our ties run closer than bloodlines, and I want everyone in the famiglia to have a decent end.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: But you, you want to put us in great danger... Anton, I think you've forgotten my teachings.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Papa, have I ever mentioned how a Perro like me ended up in Siracusa?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I was a soldier, serving the True Bolívarians.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: I have but a superficial understanding of the situation in Bolívar...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: It actually doesn't matter which flag you fight under in Bolívar. You don't have to understand why the three parties are fighting one another. I mean, everyone's just trying to survive by giving it their all.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I was in a guerrilla force raiding a village under the Singas dynasty, but we were discovered, and the entire squad became captives.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The twenty of us emptied every pocket and piled our possessions together to bribe the executioner to spare us, change our status from 'death penalty' to 'hard labor'.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The officer responsible for driving us was a paunchy aristocrat. He was drunk that day, made a mistake during the review process, and only came to us with a truck... big enough to sit just ten people.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The executioner asked him what to do next. Can you guess how that stronzo replied?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: He belched from his drink as he whipped out a pen and drew a circle on our list, saying: There's clearly only ten people on the list, right?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: We killed him, cut off his head, escaped Bolívar, and what happened next, I'm sure you know.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Anton, this is the first time I've heard of—

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Haha. It's been too long I almost forgot about it.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Do you know why it suddenly came back to me?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I was discussing with our young and promising mayor about building a logistical network in the city. He refused me, and then shared how the city came about, and its mission...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: A so-called 'experimental ground', with a new order governing people from the old, vastly different from the Siracusan tradition...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: He knew people would have trouble adapting, irreconcilable conflicts would occur, and the system might even swallow groups of people in the process... but it couldn't be helped, there was a potential future.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: And all of that happened because four young people sat at the Grey Hall's round table and lobbied for their idea so passionately...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Signora Sicilia allocated them one of Siracusa's twenty-three cities, without hesitation...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: A move so cavalier, like that aristocrat who circled half our names away.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Papa, Leontuzzo was indeed quite sincere and inspiring at the time, but I almost lost control, I wanted to burst into laughter... That boy knows nothing at all.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: You said I lost myself?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: No, not at all. What I want to do has always been the same.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I hate that aristocrat and Signora Sicilia. I hate their power to wantonly draw their circles as they please. I want to take it all away from them!

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Anton...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Phew—Alright, Papa. I've said a bit too much today. I'm not here to let you lecture me on decency or dignity, nor am I here to analyze what's going on in Siracusa.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: My activities this year alone are not enough to land a seat at the gambling table...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Papa, don't we have a landship en-route nearby? I'd like the rights to make an emergency dispatch.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: This is something only Don Venezia can do.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: If I refuse, will the men guarding the door deal with me like how you handled Carle?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Of course not, you're a truly decent man worthy of a dignified end.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: You're old, Papa. Haven't you always suggested you retire?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Scusi, is Eirene not here right now?

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: ...Y-Your Honor?

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: U-Uh, Eirene's not here. Everyone went to celebrate her acquittal, that's why.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: So why aren't you with them?

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: I-I'm just servicing these trucks. See?

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: Carnevale's tomorrow, and they'll need a lot of our cars...

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: Someone has to do it.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You're lying, Signore.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: When you see her, please let Eirene know I need to meet her, even outside of office hours.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: ...Got it.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: Eirene, here. The schedule table for this year.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: As you said, I marked all the Venezia Trucking related records. Trip times, loading instructions, driver names... they're all in there.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Yep, matches with Sommer's notebook.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Sommer wanted to bring Guri here; Carmelo was secretly nursing his injuries with alcohol and couldn't get it from us; Gianni and Ruggiero had their own troubles too...

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Every member of ours they targeted was carefully selected.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: There aren't many records, but the shipment frequency is very consistent. That night wasn't the first time they smuggled weapons into the city for sure...

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: You were right. That judge did come looking for you at the camp. After she left, some famiglie associates were tailing her in secret.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: I drove behind her car and came back here only after I saw her enter the courthouse.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: There's also one more thing.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: I happened to see Saluzzo Vino's legal team hurrying into the courthouse.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: I asked around, and apparently not long ago the police suddenly showed up at one of the Saluzzo wineries and took Alberto away.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Venezia Trucking also got the cops at their door at the same time. The police and judges should be inspecting their factories right now.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Lavinia probably doesn't know about the weapons yet, but the car accident and port fire has already sent out a dangerous signal...

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Leontuzzo's injured and still hospitalized even now. As Nuova Volsinii's Supreme Justice, she tries her best to get the situation under control.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: She didn't use a direct method with us like she did with the other two... she went to camp to warn us.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: In other words, an ultimatum.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: Wait, about what Lyudmila just said...

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Neither Alberto or Venezia Junior will willingly meet their demise.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Lavinia's in danger right now.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Those wise guys only followed her with no intentions to harm her.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: We're in Nuova Volsinii after all, we got cops patrolling the streets. Besides, they have an even better time slot available...

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: You mean Carnevale...?

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: We could let the judge know.
Eirene stays still for a long time before shaking her head.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Are you still hesitant to let her know about the Truckers' Union? But can you really just stand here and watch something happen to her?

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: She's not a bad person at least.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: You got it wrong, Lyudmila.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: It's too late for us now to stay out of it.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: If the famiglie dare make a direct attempt on Lavinia's life during Carnevale, there's no chance they'll let the Truckers' Union go. If that happens, we can only wait for the slaughter to happen.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: I'm just thinking what I should do. I don't want something like what happened with Sommer to happen again...

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Giving Lavinia a direct warning isn't the best choice here.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Lyudmila, did you see the weapons? How many were there?

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Based on the amount I saw and total number of shifts on the schedule—

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: I estimate there's enough Venezia weapons in the city to arm several tactical squads with dozens of people in each.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: We have more than two hundred registered members, but if we include ad-hoc staff and contract workers, we'll have several times the number of people.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: I just realized the Truckers' Union is actually the largest organization in Nuova Volsinii.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Maybe we can manage it. Protecting a single person in the dark.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Do you really just want to protect that judge?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Sommer taught me one thing at least: no one can be trusted in this city but ourselves.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: So we can only protect ourselves... even if that means resorting to violence.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: When I was in Ursus, I knew someone with similar ideas. She lost herself in the end.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: You want to stop me?

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: No... What happened with Sommer needs a proper ending.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: But of course, he wouldn't want to see you lose yourself either.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Eirene, I guarantee you won't cross that final line...

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: I promise you I won't, Lyudmila.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: I'm perfectly aware what I'm doing.
